transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (CTO, Novaris), Marcus Li (ML Eng), Priya Singh (SRE)

Summary: Intro to Redwood PLG quickstart, qualification of Novaris use case (clinical assistant for provider notes), discussion of hosting options (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private), security requirements, and next steps to provision trial keys and run benchmarks.

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. How are you doing today?
[00:00:07] Janelle: Hey Maya, thanks. Doing well. Appreciate you squeezing us in before the holiday week.
[00:00:12] Marcus: Yep thanks, we are excited to learn more.
[00:00:18] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda: we'll run through your goals, cover the PLG quickstart (free credits / time-to-first-token), high-level hosting options \u2014 hosted, dedicated, private \u2014 and then dig into security questions. Liam will cover some latency/cost bits and we can capture next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:30] Janelle: Sounds great.

[00:01:05] Maya: So to start, can you give us a bit of context on the project and success criteria?
[00:01:12] Janelle: Sure. We're building a clinical assistant to help physicians summarize visits and surface relevant guidelines. Main goal is to cut documentation time by 30%. We'll need PII handling, audit logs, and SSO. Early phase is small internal pilot \u2014 50 clinicians \u2014 then expand. Timeline is Q1 pilot. Success metrics are latency under 600ms tail for short prompts, and per-token cost not exploding.
[00:01:38] Priya: And for infra, we use AWS in us-east-1, VPC with strict egress rules. We prefer either hosted with VPC peering or a private deployment if required by compliance.
[00:01:50] Liam: Got it. That maps to a lot we see. The PLG quickstart is usually the fastest path to time-to-first-token: you sign up, get free credits, we give temp API keys and a sample repo to spin up locally. Typically customers have a token-limited sandbox within a day.

[00:02:20] Marcus: When you say "time-to-first-token" what do you mean operationally? How quick is realistically?
[00:02:27] Liam: In practice for the hosted API it's minutes to test inference from your workstation \u2014 assuming no org-level SSO blocks. For a more productiony setup with SSO + audit logging and possibly VPC peering, that can be a few days to a couple weeks depending on legal and security reviews. The quickstart gets you experimenting fast.
[00:02:50] Maya: Also free credits \u2014 we can provision trial credits tied to the account so you can run prompt sets up to, say, 100k tokens without charge.

[00:03:15] Janelle: Nice. One of our compliance folks asked about data retention and KMS. Do you store transcripts? Is customer data encrypted at rest?
[00:03:24] Maya: Yes \u2014 hosted stores logs for operational debugging by default but can be disabled; we have options to disable retention and we offer customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated. We are SOC 2, and we can share the whitepaper.
[00:03:40] Priya: When you say Dedicated, is that single-tenant GPUs in our VPC or in Redwood-managed region? We need network isolation.
[00:03:48] Liam: Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and can be deployed with customer VPC peering for network isolation. There's a Dedicated config with private networking and stricter retention policies. For full air-gapped on-prem we do Redwood Private. Sometimes the product names get mixed \u2014 people call it Redwood Dedictaed, ha \u2014 but it's the reserved capacity option.

[00:04:15] Marcus: How about latency tradeoffs? If we go hosted versus dedicated what's the expected difference?
[00:04:21] Liam: Hosted is multi-tenant but optimized; we publish perf profiles. For typical 1k token prompt generation we see median latencies in 150-300ms on our c5/gpu-equivalent routes, tail can be higher. Dedicated gives you predictable tail latencies and throughput; you'd avoid noisy neighbor issues and can get lower 95/99th percentiles. We also do KV cache and batching to improve per-token cost but that can add a bit of jitter.

[00:05:00] Janelle: Does batching change user-facing latency? We want interactive feel.
[00:05:06] Liam: Good question \u2014 batching helps cost but we tune policies by route. For interactive endpoints we favor low-latency configs with smaller batch windows. There's a tradeoff: more aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency. We can set per-route SLOs in the console.

[00:05:40] Maya: Another thing \u2014 most PLG customers start on hosted to validate product-market fit and then if they outgrow it or need strict compliance they migrate to Dedicated or Private. The API stays the same so it's low friction.

[00:06:05] Marcus: Ok that helps. On billing \u2014 is hosted usage-based? And how do we forecast cost per clinician?
[00:06:12] Maya: Hosted is usage-based (per-token generation and embeddings). For forecasting we recommend running a small sample of prompts and we can help model token counts. We'll also show per-token cost with and without quantization and batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize.

[00:06:38] Priya: For SSO and RBAC, do you support SAML / SCIM for provisioning? We need SCIM to auto-provision accounts.
[00:06:45] Liam: Yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. Audit logs and token-level observability are available in the Console. Some customers wire logs into their SIEM via a secure export.

[00:07:15] Janelle: What's the security review timeline usually? We have a security questionnaire that takes a bit.
[00:07:22] Maya: For most PLG trials we can answer questionnaires in a few days; a full enterprise security review for Dedicated/Private takes longer. We'll send the SOC 2 pack, encryption docs, and an architecture note for VPC peering.

[00:07:50] Marcus: We will want to run a small benchmark \u2014 500 short prompts and 100 long prompts \u2014 to validate latency and quality. Can you help with that?
[00:07:58] Liam: Absolutely. We have a benchmark template. I'll share a script you can run against the trial keys. We can also run the same test from Dedicated once you commit to reserved capacity.

[00:08:20] Janelle: One more thing \u2014 our legal is picky about vendor access to logs. Can you give us a way to opt out of Redwood support access?
[00:08:29] Maya: Yes, we have support controls and fine-grained access. You can restrict support access, and for Dedicated/Private we can set stricter control with customer-managed keys so logs are unreadable to us.

[00:09:00] Marcus: Good. Now from a dev experience standpoint \u2014 what does the quickstart repo include?
[00:09:07] Liam: The repo has an example Node/Python client, sample prompts, a simple docker compose showing a small proxy for VPC egress rules, and a script to measure token usage. It's pretty straightforward: plug in API key and hit the endpoints. People hit first token usually within 10-20 minutes if they follow the guide.

[00:09:40] Janelle: Nice. Any rate limits on trial keys?
[00:09:44] Maya: Trial keys are rate-limited to protect system stability but are sufficient for a benchmark run. If you need more throughput we can temporarily raise quotas.

[00:10:05] Marcus: You mentioned KV cache earlier \u2014 can you explain briefly what that is? I've seen it written as KV cash in some notes.
[00:10:12] Liam: (laughs) KV cache \u2014 Key-Value cache for the model's attention state when using chat-style workloads. It reduces repeated compute for prefixes, so for long conversations it's a big cost saver and can improve latency on subsequent tokens. The runtime handles it automatically for supported models.

[00:10:46] Priya: If we have egress restrictions in our VPC, how do hosted requests get through?
[00:10:51] Maya: We do VPC peering and private networking; alternatively, you can run a lightweight proxy inside your VPC that forwards requests \u2014 the quickstart repo has an example. For strict air-gap regimens Private is the option.

[00:11:20] Janelle: From a decision standpoint, what would you recommend for a pilot \u2014 hosted or dedicated?
[00:11:27] Liam: For speed-to-value start hosted PLG quickstart. It minimizes procurement friction. If you hit security gating in the pilot, we can spin a Dedicated environment for predictability and isolation.

[00:11:45] Maya: Totally. PLG path also gives you usage visibility and lets you validate per-token economics before committing.

[00:12:10] Marcus: Are there preview features or function-calling-like capabilities? We want structured outputs for clinical codes.
[00:12:17] Liam: We support structured outputs and function/tool calling patterns; you can return JSON schemas and our SDKs parse structured responses. If you need strict output validation, we have recommended patterns.

[00:12:45] Priya: Any concerns about PHI?
[00:12:49] Maya: PHI handling is a common ask. Hosted can be configured with data retention disabled and customer-managed keys, but some customers require Private or on-prem for PHI. We can discuss specifics with security/legal.

[00:13:10] Janelle: Okay great. Let's talk logistics \u2014 what do you need from us to get started with the quickstart?
[00:13:17] Maya: Minimal: a point of contact, an email to tie trial credits to, and a small prompt set for benchmarking. For SSO, your IdP metadata if you want SSO enabled for the trial org.

[00:13:32] Marcus: We can provide prompts and token estimates. Priya will coordinate SSO later.

[00:13:40] Maya: Awesome. Liam I'll hand to you to go over a quick perf/benchmark plan and the test script.

[00:13:46] Liam: Cool. I'm sharing screen now \u2014 (screen share noise) \u2014
[00:13:55] [screen noise, brief silence]
[00:14:10] Liam: Alright the benchmark plan: small prompt latency test (500 queries, 8-16 tokens output), long prompt test (100 queries, 600-1200 tokens), and a concurrency test to gauge throughput. We'll include exact curl/python commands, and a script that emits timestamps for p99 calculation. We'll also capture token counts.

[00:15:05] Marcus: That looks good. Do you instrument for tail latencies?
[00:15:09] Liam: Yes \u2014 script gives median and p95/p99. For hosted we've observed p99 variance due to batching and multi-tenant load but generally it's within SLA for most interactive apps. If you need consistent p99 < 600ms we recommend Dedicated or smaller model selection.
[00:15:40] Janelle: Model selection \u2014 do you curate model options? We want to balance quality and cost.
[00:15:46] Maya: We maintain a model catalog with recommended profiles; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles per workload. We can recommend a smaller quantized variant for inference to reduce cost while preserving quality in many cases.

[00:16:20] Marcus: Ok. On the security docs, can you send SOC2 and the encryption + KMS doc?
[00:16:25] Maya: Yes will do. I'll attach them in the follow-up.

[00:16:40] Priya: For audit trails do you keep token-level logs? We need per-request metadata for audits.
[00:16:46] Liam: We store request metadata (timestamps, route, model, tokens). Content logs are optional and can be disabled. For Dedicated/Private exportable logs integrate into your SIEM.

[00:17:20] Janelle: Hypothetical procurement question \u2014 if this goes well and we need Dedicated, what's the usual contract cadence?
[00:17:27] Maya: Dedicated typically moves to reserved monthly or annual commitments; we can provide pricing tiers and a playbook. For pilots you can stay on hosted until commitment.

[00:18:00] Marcus: Anything we should watch for when running the scripts?
[00:18:04] Liam: Ensure you run from the same region (us-east-1) and disable local proxies that could add jitter. We'll provide a controlled runner.

[00:18:30] Janelle: Ok cool. I want to understand what the support model looks like during pilot.

[00:18:36] Maya: PLG customers get community + docs; we provide lightweight onboarding from Solutions Engineering for trials. If you sign for Dedicated we'll include a named CSM and support SLA.

[00:19:00] Priya: Any regulatory certifications beyond SOC 2? ISO?
[00:19:05] Maya: We have SOC 2; ISO is in our roadmap \u2014 I'll check status and include in the pack.

[00:19:30] Marcus: Do you have a sandbox dataset for clinical testing or does it need to be our prompts?
[00:19:35] Liam: We provide generic healthcare prompt templates but it's best to test with your real prompts (masked/anon) to measure real token patterns.

[00:20:00] Janelle: Alright let's capture next steps.

[00:20:05] Maya: I'll summarize: 1) Maya to send quickstart guide, free credits instructions, SOC2 and security docs; 2) Liam to share benchmark script and runbook; 3) Novaris to send prompt set and IdP metadata if they want SSO enabled for trial; 4) Schedule benchmark run next week.

[00:20:32] Marcus: That works.

[00:20:40] Priya: I may follow up with some very specific network questions.

[00:20:45] Maya: Totally \u2014 we'll handle that. Anything else?

[00:20:50] Janelle: No, that's it. Appreciate the clarity.

[00:21:10] Liam: Quick note on cost optimisation \u2014 after you run the pilot we can run Redwood Optimize suggestions and give a short report showing expected monthly spend at different scales.

[00:21:20] Marcus: Great.

[00:21:35] Maya: Okay we'll get the docs over today and the trial keys set up. For the trial keys I'll create an org and give you an admin key Marcus, or Janelle \u2014 which email should we tie it to?
[00:21:45] Janelle: Use janelle.ortiz@novarishealth.com.

[00:21:50] Maya: Perfect. I'll follow up with the invite and the quickstart link.

[00:22:05] Marcus: Thanks everyone.

[00:22:12] Priya: Thanks.

[00:22:20] Maya: Closing notes: expect an email with attached SOC2 and quickstart, free credits provisioned within 24 hours, and Liam will post the benchmark script. We'll pencil in a benchmarking sesh next Thursday.

[00:22:41] Janelle: Sounds good.

[00:23:00] (Call ends, informal wrap)

Notes on transcription: occasional downstream garbling of product names (Redwood Dedictaed, KV cash) and minor speaker overlap.
